The mapping is `ESCALATION_BY_KIND` in `apps/api/src/tools/defineTmsTool.ts`, the `defineTmsTool` factory. It is a `Record<TmsErrorKind, EscalationTrigger | null>` covering the nine `TmsError` kinds. A kind with no row fails `npm run typecheck`. It replaced a nine-way `switch`, which the repo's `complexity` and `re-lint/prefer-polymorphism` lint rules reject.

Two kinds escalate. `unavailable` (5xx) maps to `tms_unavailable`, and `timeout` maps to `tms_timeout`. The factory also marks the trigger on the turn's escalation recorder.

The other seven kinds map to null and do not escalate. They are `not_found`, `rate_limited`, `network`, `invalid_response`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden` and `unexpected`. I took the last of these from the spec's open-question text, not from a full list of the nine.

The `get_booking_status` contract also lists a separate `customer_scope_conflict` escalation. It is not a TMS error kind. It fires when a shipment's customer contradicts its order's customer, and the factory marks it.

The spec leaves open whether `unauthorized`, `forbidden`, `invalid_response` and `unexpected` should escalate, since a server-side fault leaves no human informed.

judgements.reason: The answer names the right location but says only two kinds escalate and claims customer_scope_conflict is not a TMS error kind, while the gold lists it as a third escalating kind.
